page.after:
What the differences mean

The size line was drawn at about 20% either side of 4,000 Wh. The BLUETTI Elite 400 kits (3,840 Wh) sit well inside it. The ALLPOWERS R3500 kits (3,168 Wh, 20.8% under) sit on its edge and are included because they are the kits in this table that ship today. Left out: the Anker SOLIX S5000 + 2× 400 W kit (5,024 Wh, 25.6% over) and the BLUETTI Elite 300 kits (3,014.4 Wh, 24.6% under).

  • Price per Wh is the price through our link divided by the rated battery. R3500 + 600 W: $1,753.93 / 3,168 Wh = $0.554. Elite 400 + 2× 200 W: $1,804.05 / 3,840 Wh = $0.470. The BLUETTI kit costs $50.12 more and holds 672 Wh more, but ships about two months later.
  • Refill hours are battery Wh divided by panel watts at rated output; real panel output is lower. R3500 + 600 W: 3,168 / 600 = 5.3 h. Elite 400 + 2× 200 W: 3,840 / 400 = 9.6 h.
  • One sunny day, assuming 4.5 peak-sun hours and 85% charging efficiency: 600 × 4.5 × 0.85 = 2,295 Wh, which is 72% of the R3500. 400 × 4.5 × 0.85 = 1,530 Wh, which is 48% of the R3500 or 40% of the Elite 400.
  • Cost of the bigger panel set. R3500, 400 W to 600 W: ($1,753.93 − $1,586.73) / 200 W = $0.84 per added watt. Elite 400, 2× 200 W to 2× 350 W: ($2,325.60 − $1,804.05) / 300 W = $1.74 per added watt.
  • Kit against the same parts at BLUETTI's store on 2026-11-18, all as pre-orders: the 2× 200 W kit is $398 less, the 2× 350 W kit $349 less, the 350 W kit $299 less and the 500 W kit $99 less.

Price per Wh and refill hours beside the EcoFlow and Jackery kits

EcoFlow's and Jackery's US stores refused our price requests on 2026-11-18, so their kits are not rows in the table. StormWatts' dated reads of those stores give the scale, with the same arithmetic applied:

  • EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 + 400 W (4,096 Wh): StormWatts read $3,099 on 2026-10-16. $3,099 / 4,096 = $0.757 per Wh; 4,096 / 400 = 10.2 h. PowerSized reported EcoFlow's DELTA Pro 3 solar kits out of stock on 2026-11-17.
  • Jackery HomePower 3600 Plus + 2× SolarSaga 200 W (3,584 Wh): StormWatts read $2,549 on 2026-11-08. $2,549 / 3,584 = $0.711 per Wh; 3,584 / 400 = 9.0 h. Jackery's listing on 2026-11-18 says the black station is a pre-order shipping by Dec 15 and the Red Cross Edition is in stock.
  • EcoFlow DELTA 3800 Gen4 + 4× 160 W (3,763 Wh): StormWatts read $2,599 on 2026-11-08, shipping late November. $2,599 / 3,763 = $0.691 per Wh; 3,763 / 640 = 5.9 h.

On those figures the R3500 + 600 W kit is 27% lower per Wh than the DELTA Pro 3 + 400 W kit ($0.554 against $0.757), and the Elite 400 + 2× 200 W kit is 38% lower ($0.470 against $0.757).

ALLPOWERS' listing gives the R3500 a 3,200 W inverter with a 7,000 W peak, over 3,500 charging cycles and a 2,000 W solar ceiling, so the 600 W kit uses 30% of what the station can take. The same listing sells a variant with two SP039 panels (1,200 W) at a store price of $2,562.15 on 2026-11-18, before any code: 3,168 / 1,200 = 2.6 h at rated output.

BLUETTI's page gives the Elite 400 one solar input: 1,000 W maximum, 12–60 V, 20 A. BLUETTI's 200 W panel is listed at 24.6 V open-circuit and 10.8 A short-circuit, so two in series are 49.2 V, inside the 60 V limit, and the full 400 W can reach the station; two in parallel would be 21.6 A, over the 20 A limit. The kit page does not name the panel model, so this check assumes the kit ships BLUETTI's own 200 W panel.

All capacities here are rated. StorageReview (Dylan Bryan, 2026-11-02) measured 3.07 kWh delivered from the Elite 400 on a full discharge, 80% of its 3,840 Wh rating; on that figure the 2× 200 W kit is $1,804.05 / 3,070 = $0.59 per delivered Wh. Dealectric does not test units: every figure on this page is a maker's published number, a named reviewer's measurement, or arithmetic from them.

Not recommended: BLUETTI Elite 400 + 2× 350 W

This kit has the most panel watts of the Elite 400 kits, but the station cannot take all of them. BLUETTI lists its 350 W panel at 33 V open-circuit. Two in series are 2 × 33 V = 66 V, above the Elite 400's 60 V input limit, so they have to be wired in parallel. In parallel the input's 20 A limit caps power below 20 A × 33 V = 660 W, because a panel's working voltage is always under its open-circuit voltage. The refill is therefore at least 3,840 / 660 = 5.8 h, not the 5.5 h the 700 W rating suggests.

It costs $521.55 more than the 2× 200 W kit, $1.74 per added rated watt. The ALLPOWERS R3500 + 600 W kit refills in 5.3 h at rated output for $571.67 less ($2,325.60 − $1,753.93) and ships now, with 672 Wh less battery.
